entry.title: Higher operator product expansions in twisted non-Lorentzian field theories
entry.summary: Twisting theories with super-Poincaré symmetry yields topological-holomorphic field theories, whose operator product expansions of local operators can have as coefficients not only ordinary functions but also `derived' functions with nonzero cohomological degree, described by certain elements of sheaf cohomology. Twisting non-Lorentzian supersymmetric theories yields richer phenomena, where topological and holomorphic spacetime coordinates coexist with ordinary (that is, neither topological nor holomorphic) spacetime coordinates. We propose a sheaf-cohomological description of such OPE coefficients for quantum field theories with arbitrary numbers of topological, holomorphic, and/or ordinary spacetime dimensions, and identify necessary and sufficient conditions for the proposed OPE coefficient space to contain nontrivial `derived' functions; in particular, theories with one topological spacetime dimension and multiple ordinary spacetime dimensions provide a smooth analogue of the (holomorphic) raviolo. We then demonstrate that two-point functions in topological twists of free supersymmetric non-Lorentzian field theories appearing in the literature define nontrivial derived functions consistent with our sheaf-theoretic construction.
entry.arxiv:comment: 23 pages, 2 figures. Extensive revision with explicit non-Lorentzian examples

entry.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
entry.summary: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.

entry.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
entry.summary: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_μ$ and $L_e-L_τ$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. This version corresponds to the accepted manuscript. 23 pages, 6 figures

entry.title: Fractionalized Fermi liquids with the ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz
entry.summary: Fractionalized Fermi liquids ($\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$), elusive metallic states characterized by fractionalized quasiparticles alongside conventional ones and defying Luttinger's theorem, are prime candidates for the pseudogap regime of underdoped cuprates. We show that a $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$ phase emerges in the single-band $t$-$J$ model through a simple ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz, optimized at the cost of a mean-field calculation. The resulting temperature-doping phase diagram encompasses a low-doping $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$, a $d$-wave superconducting dome, and an overdoped conventional Fermi liquid, thereby reproducing key qualitative features of cuprate phenomenology.
entry.arxiv:comment: 5 pages of main text with 2 figures, and 12 pages of supplemental material

entry.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
entry.summary: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.

entry.title: Electric birefringence in Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics
entry.summary: The fermion sector of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics is integrated functionally to generate a non-linear electrodynamics, that it is called Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics. A non-local Chern-Simons topological term is added to the original lagrangian of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics in which a most complete electrodynamics gauge invariant in 1+2 dimensions is proposed. As consequence of the fermionic sector, we obtain a non-linear contribution in the electromagnetic fields that breaks the Lorentz symmetry due to Fermi velocity. From the Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics, we study the properties of the plane wave propagating in a planar medium under an uniform and constant electromagnetic background field. The properties of the planar material are discussed through the electric permittivity tensor and magnetic permeability, that are functions of the frequency, wavelength and of the background fields. The dispersion relations and the refractive index are calculated in the presence of a uniform magnetic field, and also in the case only of an electric background field. The birefringence phenomenon emerges only when the electric background field is considered.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages, no figures. Accepted version in Nuclear Physics, section B

entry.title: Mott transitions in Dirac nodal-line semimetals
entry.summary: Nodal-line semimetals provide a natural setting to investigate how the geometry of a nodal manifold affects interaction-driven quantum phase transitions. Here, we study the Hubbard model on a cubic lattice supporting either nodal-point (cubic $π$-flux model) or nodal-line semimetallic states using mean-field theory, determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, and a weak-coupling renormalization-group (RG) analysis. In both cases, antiferromagnetic order develops only above a finite interaction strength, with the nodal-line system exhibiting a smaller critical coupling due to its enhanced low-energy density of states and markedly stronger finite-size effects. For the nodal-point model, the quantum critical behavior is compatible with $(3+1)$-dimensional Gross--Neveu mean-field scaling. In contrast, the weak-coupling RG reveals that the nodal line itself is unstable against interactions: although the Hubbard interaction is perturbatively irrelevant, its second-order self-energy generates a symmetry-allowed relevant term proportional to $U^2\cos k_z$, reconstructing the nodal line into isolated, strongly anisotropic nodal points. This weak-coupling reconstruction is distinct from the strong-coupling antiferromagnetic transition and highlights the role of nodal-manifold geometry in interacting semimetals.

entry.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
entry.summary: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.

entry.title: Shear, vorticity, and $f(R)$ theories
entry.summary: We study how an extended spherical collapse model (ESCM), including shear, vorticity and chameleon screening, modifies the collapse threshold $δ_c(z)$ and $δ_c(M)$, the turnaround density $δ_t$, the turnaround radius $R_t$ and the halo mass function in the Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ model, and whether these quantities can distinguish $f(R)$ from General Relativity (GR). Unlike the standard spherical collapse model (SSCM), in the ESCM $δ_c$ depends on mass, redshift and $|f_{R0}|$; we use it to compute the halo mass function with the excursion set approach. Between GR and the large-field (LF) limit of $f(R)$, $δ_c$ differs by a few percent within the ESCM and by about 20% between GR in the ESCM and the LF limit in the SSCM; $δ_t$ differs by about 27-29% and $R_t$ by about 6.5%. With screening, the difference between GR and screened $δ_c$ is 2.5% for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-4}$ (F4) and vanishes for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-6}$ (F6); for $δ_t$ it is larger than 20% (F4), about 10% (F5) and 0 (F6); for $R_t$ about 6.5% (F4), 3% (F5) and 0 (F6). Since observations exclude F4 and F6 is practically identical to GR, only F5 could discriminate, but the ~20% uncertainty on measured turnaround radii rules out $R_t$ and related quantities as tests of $f(R)$. The halo abundance predicted by $f(R)$, especially at high redshift, can instead distinguish $f(R)$ from GR.
entry.arxiv:comment: 23 pages, 9 figures. Published in Phys. Rev. D

entry.title: Astrophysics equation of state inference with Bayesian chiral effective field theory uncertainties
entry.summary: We investigate Bayesian chiral effective field theory ($χ$EFT) uncertainties, which assign a statistical interpretation to equation of state (EOS) distributions near nuclear saturation density, n$_0$, as well as constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) to Bayesian EOS inference from LIGO/Virgo, NICER and pulsar mass observations. The tails of the $χ$EFT uncertainties allow for broader pressure ranges in our priors, but large parts of these are excluded by the astrophysical observations, so that the EOS and the resulting mass-radius posteriors are still very consistent with our earlier work. Within our broad prior ranges, we observe a clear stiffening of the EOS at $n \gtrsim 3 n_0$. Moreover, the impact of the pQCD constraints on the posterior EOS and mass-radius range is negligible due to the astrophysics constraints. Exploiting the strong correlation between pure neutron matter and matter in beta equilibrium, we infer the symmetry energy slope parameter $L$ from astrophysics. For the $68\%$ credible interval, we obtain $L=42.6-52$ MeV and $L=44.2-56.7$ MeV using piecewise-polytrope and speed-of-sound high-density extensions, respectively. The $L$ posterior is mainly driven by the combination of GW170817 LIGO/Virgo and PSR J0740+6620, PSR J0437-4715, and PSR J0614-3329 NICER observations.
entry.arxiv:comment: 18 pages, 17 figures, 1 table. Published version at ApJ

entry.title: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
entry.summary: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Submitted to AAS Journals

entry.title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
entry.summary: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.

entry.title: Static Black Holes and Iyer-Wald Entropy in $f(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{K})$ Gravity
entry.summary: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in a class of {nonpolynomial} gravitational theories described by a {Lagrangian $f=-X^{1-n}$, where $X = \mathcal{R} + \sqrt{6\mathcal{K} - \mathcal{R}^2}$ is a function of the Ricci and Kretschmann scalars.} The modified Einstein equations contain {nonpolynomial} curvature terms. We develop a perturbative scheme to look for a black hole solution that deviates parametrically from the Schwarzschild geometry. We obtain first-order corrections to the metric by solving the resulting coupled differential equations. The corresponding Iyer--Wald entropy is then evaluated consistently to first order in the perturbative coupling. We show that the {nonpolynomial} contribution gives rise to a power-law correction to the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy.
entry.arxiv:comment: Revised version incorporating corrections to the sign of the source tensor, the resulting modifications to the perturbative solutions, and additional clarifications following peer review

entry.title: A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars
entry.summary: Recent data from cosmological galaxy surveys combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data give a preference for a departure from $Λ$CDM, favoring a model with an evolving dark energy equation of state or a small neutrino mass. However, recent works have shown that the electron scattering optical depth to the CMB ($τ$) can reduce this preference if $τ\sim0.09$, larger than that preferred by CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data. With standard monotonic hydrogen reionization histories, such a high value of $τ$ is in strong tension with spectroscopic galaxy data constraining the end of reionization. Thus, high-$τ$ models are restricted to non-standard reionization scenarios, where astrophysical sources inject an appreciable amount of ionizing photons at early times. One recently studied model for this is a supermassive population III star scenario, where radiative feedback from a self-annihilating dark matter particle enables a pathway to form $M\sim10^5 M_\odot$ stars that, upon collapse, photoionize a surrounding volume large enough to source appreciable contributions to $τ$ as a population. Here we present the first self-consistent treatment of the feedback from these supermassive population III stars within a large semi-numerical cosmological simulation, accounting for their ionizing, Lyman-Werner, and X-ray feedback on the intergalactic medium. We use it to predict the distinct signatures on the large-scale 21 cm signal at Cosmic Dawn, and forecast its detectability. We find that the 21 cm power spectrum probed by future radio survey arrays like the Square Kilometre Array could detect signatures of these supermassive population III at high significance and set model-dependent constraints on $τ$ that approach $σ_τ\sim0.012$, enough to distinguish our fiducial $τ\sim0.097$ scenario from current Planck values at $>3σ$.

entry.title: Transient early reionization allows for a high optical depth while remaining consistent with kSZ measurements
entry.summary: Recent works have shown that a CMB optical depth of $τ\approx0.09$, above the Planck low-$\ell$ polarization value of 0.054, would weaken the preference of DESI data for dynamical dark energy and for a low neutrino mass. Apart from the low-$\ell$ CMB, another probe that prefers a $τ\sim0.055$ is the kinetic Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect when combined with the end of hydrogen reionization as measured by the Ly$α$ forest. In this work we use a new self-consistent model of supermassive Population~III stars, which partially ionize the intergalactic medium at high redshifts ($z\approx20$--$25$), to predict the kSZ signal. We show that such an early, transient reionization phase can raise $τ$ to $\approx0.09$ while remaining consistent with current kSZ and Ly-$α$ forest constraints. We forecast that the Simons Observatory, combined with Ly-$α$ forest and UV luminosity function data, can constrain the optical depth accumulated above $z=12$ to $\pm0.008$ in our fiducial supermassive Pop~III scenario.

entry.title: PSR J1807-2459B in NGC 6544: A Unique Relativistic Binary in a Dense Cluster
entry.summary: The globular cluster NGC 6544 is a high-density, dynamically evolved system located in the direction of the Galactic Center, known for hosting the eccentric binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1807-2459B. We present a new timing solution for this pulsar, based on more than 26 years of observations with the Parkes, Green Bank and MeerKAT radio telescopes. We measure for the first time the variation of the orbital period, which is dominated by the acceleration of the binary in the cluster potential: this places the pulsar in front of the cluster center and reveals its intrinsic spin-down, typical of a fully recycled millisecond pulsar. We also improve the measurements of the rate of advance of periastron and of the Einstein delay, the latter by a factor of four, and include the previously neglected contributions of the proper motion, which makes these parameters and the derived masses of the pulsar and its companion, $1.3636^{+0.0017}_{-0.0021}\,M_\odot$ and $1.2071^{+0.0021}_{-0.0017}\,M_\odot$, more realistic. Together with the Shapiro delay, these measurements allow two independent tests of general relativity, both passed. Our results show that precise post-Keplerian parameters of a binary pulsar in a dense cluster can probe both the cluster gravitational field and general relativity, provided that kinematic effects are carefully taken into account.

entry.title: What Can Next Generation Ultrafast Light Sources Tell Us About Quantum Materials?
entry.summary: Ultrafast spectroscopy of quantum materials has emerged as a principle application of modern ultrafast optical sources. Measurements made with ultrashort pulses allow the normally strongly coupled internal degrees of freedom inside these systems to be de-coupled in the time-domain, revealing the key interactions for the different orders that lead to dramatic emergent phenomena. This has naturally motivated a wide range of experiments, and quantum materials have now been studied with ultrafast sources spanning from the hard X-ray to the THz, with fields intense enough to create non-equilibrium states, and using pulses down to the attosecond duration. As the optical spectroscopist's toolbox becomes increasingly complete, it is worth pausing and reflecting on what are the capabilities that we currently lack for examining quantum materials, and what are the problems that require the next generation of ultrafast sources now coming on-line or being designed. Here I will offer an overview of the remaining missing capabilities in ultrafast optical sources as required for studying quantum materials, and identify some outstanding problems where I believe these new sources can provide decisive impact in our understanding of quantum and strongly-correlated materials.

entry.title: Amplifying the Cosmological Collider with Ghost Spectators
entry.summary: Ghost inflation is a well-known framework in which cosmological fluctuations can generate enhanced primordial non-Gaussianity, typically of the equilateral type. In its original form, however, it is in tension with current observational constraints. Here we instead consider a setup in which a standard inflaton drives the background evolution, while excitations of a ghost condensate act as spectator fields that interact with the inflaton. This proposal fits naturally within the cosmological collider program: the exchanged particle has a modified dispersion relation, $ω\propto k^2$. We show that this ghost-inspired dynamics weakens the usual Boltzmann suppression, similarly to models with a very small effective sound speed, yielding an enhanced bispectrum signal relative to standard cosmological collider scenarios. At the same time, the horizon-crossing scale remains a free parameter of the theory. As a result, the model shares features of both the de Sitter bootstrap and boostless frameworks. Finally, we derive the differential equations governing cosmological correlators in the ghost-collider setup. Their structure reflects the quadratic momentum dependence of the dispersion relation and distinguishes this scenario from conventional relativistic cases.

entry.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
entry.summary: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Photometric-redshift pipeline overview and validation
entry.summary: We present the pipeline design of the photometric redshift processing function for Data Release 1 (DR1) of the $Euclid$ mission, and the validation and performance of our cosmology-related products that are released as part of DR1-Foundation. The $Euclid$ mission aims to constrain the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy, $w$, to percent-level accuracy through the measurement of large-scale structure via weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. As part of DR1-Foundation we release determinations of photometric redshifts (photo-$z$), corrected photometry, and object classes that are used to form the basis of the cosmological samples. The release furthermore includes estimates of the spectral energy distributions of stars and galaxies for the careful modelling of the point-spread function for weak-lensing measurement. We estimate the performance of the photo-$z$ point estimates and probability distribution functions using overlapping spectroscopic redshifts, which are weighted to match different flux-limited target samples. We find that the current performance is somewhat below mission design requirements ($40\%$ in scatter and a factor of 2 in outlier fraction) at the nominal survey depth ($I_{\rm E}<24.5$), but closely matching requirements at slightly brighter magnitudes ($I_{\rm E}<24$), consistent with pre-launch analyses and the slightly shallower external data (up to $0.3\,\mathrm{mag}$) with respect to end-of-mission expectations. Data from Rubin-LSST will help alleviate this issue by the time of the final cosmology analyses. The other cosmology-related outputs are tested to the extent that is possible with currently available comparison data. This paper is partnered by an article describing the measurement of the physical properties of galaxies for the purpose of non-cosmological science.
entry.arxiv:comment: Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

entry.title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
entry.summary: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically non-perturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality, characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd$_2$(Si$_{1-x}$Ge$_x$)$_2$, where, depending on $x$ and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for $x \approx 0.1$ by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

entry.title: Very High-Energy GRB Afterglow Fits with Neural-Network Emulation and Bayesian inference
entry.summary: The very high-energy ($E > 100$ GeV) afterglow emission in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) can be explained by synchrotron self-Compton (SSC). Modeling this emission accurately requires fully numerical codes that solve the time-dependent coupled particle--photon kinetic equations while accounting for Klein--Nishina suppression. However, their substantial computational cost makes them impractical for traditional parameter inference techniques such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. In this work, we present a highly efficient surrogate model based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) that emulates a one-zone kinetic SSC radiation code. To train our ANN, we use a multi-dimensional model parameter grid that constitutes a sample of 100,800 spectra produced by an infinitely thin spherical blast wave propagating inside a constant density interstellar medium (ISM). The ANN reproduces the numerical spectra well, with the median relative error generally below 2 per cent across the full frequency domain. Using this surrogate framework, we perform Bayesian parameter posterior estimation via MCMC and fit the broadband GRB afterglow observations of GRB 190114C from X-rays to TeV $γ$-rays at different epochs. We find an energetic jet with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k,iso}\simeq7.2\times10^{54}$ erg moving with a coasting bulk Lorentz factor of $Γ\gtrsim500$ into an ISM with density $n\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$. The deviation of our model light curve from observations on long timescales suggests that an ISM environment is inconsistent, and instead favours a radially stratified external medium.

entry.title: Fortuitous ABJM Operators as Black Holes
entry.summary: Given a superconformal gauge theory at a fixed loop order, BPS states can be studied in two ways --- by enumerating cohomology classes of a nilpotent supercharge or by diagonalizing the anomalous dimension matrix. The second one allows for a deeper look at how holographic theories distinguish between operators based on whether they are dual to horizonless geometries or black holes. To this end, we carry out the diagonalization in $\mathrm{U}(N)_k \times \mathrm{U}(N)_{-k}$ ABJM theory with $N$ as a formal parameter. This makes it possible to define trajectories of operators and focus on the fortuitous ones which are characterized by being BPS at only finitely many values of $N$. In contrast to $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills, where it has been numerically prohibitive to study more than one of these, ABJM gives us access to 16 such trajectories along with their descendants. We show that they take an especially simple form at large $N$ where they agree with the predictions of integrability. We also show that many of them, as with black holes, can only be dressed by certain types of gravitons and comment on how this exercise in cohomology also has implications for properties of the full operators. Finally, we show that the gap to the first non-BPS state in ABJM theory qualitatively differs from that of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills in the expected way.
entry.arxiv:comment: 64 pages, 15 figures, v2: Added corrections and a discussion of generalized monotonicity

entry.title: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
entry.summary: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. We show that this makes elastically scattering anapole dark matter a viable interpretation of the single high-energy nuclear-recoil event recorded by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, in a region where almost no background is expected. Curiously, the same coupling that fits the LZ data also yields the observed dark matter abundance at a mass of about 300 GeV, and is consistent with collider searches and indirect detection. The scenario is testable, predicting further events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will probe and a next-generation detector such as XLZD will decisively test.

entry.title: Extension of Poincare superalgebra via hidden symmetries
entry.summary: Isometries of a manifold and special types of spinors called Killing spinors which are related to Killing vector fields constitute a symmetry superalgebra structure corresponding to Poincare superalgebra. The antisymmetric generalization of Killing vector fields to higher degree forms which are called Killing-Yano forms are considered. The odd part of the Poincare superalgebra is extended from the space of Killing vector fields and their rotational representation to the space of special odd Killing-Yano forms and special even closed conformal Killing-Yano forms. The even part is again corresponds to the space of Killing spinors. By defining the relevant brackets, we show that hidden symmetries and Killing spinors together define an extension of the Poincare superalgebra.

entry.title: What Hall Measures in Strongly Correlated Metals
entry.summary: The Hall effect provides a sensitive probe of electronic correlations in strongly interacting metals, yet its microscopic interpretation beyond quasiparticle transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a Liouvillian formulation of the Hall conductivity that organizes the response into different classes of flux-sensitive many-body interference operators. Using a Schrieffer-Wolff transformation of the Hubbard model, we identify how projected charge motion and virtual hopping processes contribute to oriented trajectories enclosing magnetic flux. A high-temperature expansion reveals a hierarchy of inverse-temperature contributions associated with these interference processes. This framework provides a possible microscopic interpretation of the integer power laws previously observed in determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, which emerge at temperatures below the regime where the expansion is formally controlled. Our results highlight the sensitivity of Hall transport to coherent many-body dynamics and establish a connection between lattice geometry, electronic correlations, and transverse charge response.

entry.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
entry.summary: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.

entry.title: Degeneracies in the quasinormal mode spectrum of the Kerr-Sen black hole
entry.summary: The non-Hermitian nature of the eigenvalue problem underlying black hole perturbations can induce the presence of exceptional points (EPs) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. EPs are points in parameter space where QNMs become degenerate. Near an EP, QNMs are resonantly excited, leaving imprints on the ringdown signal. In this work, we investigate the exceptional structure of scalar perturbations of the Kerr-Sen black hole, a rotating, charged solution of the low-energy limit of heterotic string theory, and compare it with the EP structure of the Kerr-Newman black hole in General Relativity. Starting from the EP associated with a massive scalar field in the Kerr limit, we trace exceptional lines in the parameter space spanned by the black hole spin, charge, and field mass. We locate these degeneracies directly by imposing double-root conditions on the QNM secular equation, thus avoiding the need for parameter space scans. We also investigate the hysteresis phenomenon, showing that encircling an EP in parameter space leads to an exchange of the associated QNMs.

author.name: Sérgio V. M. C. B. Xavier

entry.title: Anatomy of LyC Escape in MEGATRON: Connecting Feedback Physics to Demographics, Leakage Timescales, and Explorations of ISM Density as a Tracer of Escape Fraction
entry.summary: Constraining the Lyman Continuum (LyC) escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$) of high-redshift galaxies is essential to connect the abundant populations revealed by \textit{JWST} to cosmic reionization. We investigate this interplay using {\small MEGATRON}, a suite of zoom simulations with detailed radiation/chemistry and varied feedback prescriptions. We find that feedback physics simultaneously regulates UV source counts, LyC escape fractions, and escaping ionizing luminosities ($\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$), producing different reionization histories. These differences are governed by the delay between a starburst and LyC escape: efficient early feedback and lower-density environments enable photons to escape while pre-supernovae stellar populations remain strongly ionizing. Consequently, models that produce fewer UV-bright galaxies yield earlier LyC escape and reionize sooner than models with more abundant UV sources and delayed LyC emission. Furthermore, UV-faint galaxies follow a common physical sequence in ISM structure with increasing $f_{\rm esc}$ irrespective of feedback physics: stronger leakers ($1\%\leq f_{\rm esc}\leq 50\%$) exhibit evidence of strong photoionization and SNe feedback alongside post-starburst star formation histories, while extreme leakers ($f_{\rm esc}\geq 50\%$) have also cleared their cold/dense ISM. We find that electron densities inferred from the $\rm [O\,{II}]\,λ\lambda3727$ doublet are a candidate diagnostic of $f_{\rm esc}$, with lower densities around $\rm H~{\small II}$ regions selecting stronger leakers. Moreover, this density can trace the early evolution of $f_{\rm esc}$, whereas UV slope-based calibrations over-predict $\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$ for individual young galaxies by up to two orders of magnitude. Overall, the delayed duty cycle of LyC leakage must be accounted for when UV source counts are interpreted in the context of reionization.
entry.arxiv:comment: 24 pages, 15 figures, 3 appendices (3 figures). Comments are very welcome!

entry.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
entry.summary: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio ζ_\parallel/η_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available ζ_\parallel/s, η_\parallel/s plots.
entry.arxiv:comment: 6 pages main + 12 pages supplemental material, 5 figures, LaTeX

entry.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
entry.summary: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

entry.title: Exact Infrared Triangle in Gravity with Long-Range Interactions
entry.summary: Einstein gravity coupled to massless matter exhibits universality in the infrared. In the presence of long-range interactions we show that a novel superrotation charge conservation is equivalent to the massless limit of the classical logarithmic soft graviton theorem, and we propose a formula for the corresponding tail to the displacement memory. These results, which extend earlier work on gravity coupled to massive matter in a qualitatively different way, are exact in the gravitational coupling and reveal that long-range gravitational dressings resum. We also compute higher-order corrections to the known superrotation charge which are exact in the gravitational coupling and would correspond to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo-Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.

entry.title: Searching for Massive Scalar Fields with non-minimal Curvature Couplings in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Ringdown Signals
entry.summary: We search for massive scalar fields with non-minimal curvature couplings using the loudest ringdown signals observed by LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA. We find that current ringdown observations do not provide informative constraints on the scalar-field mass. We nevertheless constrain the coupling length scale for scalar fields satisfying $Mμ<1$, where $μ$ is the scalar-field mass, yielding marginalized 90$\%$ credible upper limits of 60.4 km and 59.8 km for dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet couplings, respectively.

entry.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
entry.summary: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

entry.title: FastBox: A lightweight Python package for rapid cosmological 21cm intensity mapping simulations
entry.summary: FastBox is a Python package for generating fast, physically realistic simulations of cosmological signals in three-dimensional co-moving boxes, with the primary focus of its application being 21cm intensity mapping (IM) experiments. It provides a framework for producing cosmology-dependent Gaussian and log-normal density fields, as well as modelling the effects of redshift-space distortions and linear biasing, among others. Models of instrumental systematics are incorporated, including radiometer noise and beam convolutions. Diffuse and point source foreground models are included, along with a number of foreground filtering strategies such as PCA, ICA, and transfer function correction via mock signal injection. Lastly, estimators are provided for power spectra, the two-point correlation function, and the equilateral bispectrum. The same underlying density field can also be Poisson-sampled into a discrete galaxy catalogue, so that 21cm and galaxy tracers are simulated from common initial conditions and their cross-power spectrum can be measured. Simulation grids may be cubic or anisotropic, with independent side lengths and cell counts along each Cartesian axis. FastBox is designed as a lightweight but realistic test-bench for the development and validation of end-to-end cosmological analysis pipelines.

entry.title: An analytic diffusion model for viewing-angle effects in explosive transients
entry.summary: The tight observed relation between the peak bolometric luminosity, $L_{\mathrm p}$, and the width ratio $L_{30}/L_{\mathrm p}$ of Type Ia supernovae, with $L_{30}$ the luminosity 30 d after explosion, makes viewing-angle effects a useful test of explosion models. We develop an analytic diffusion model for homologously expanding asymmetric ejecta with uniform density and grey opacity, based on a Green's-function solution and an Eddington surface-emission prescription, and obtain angle-dependent light curves for a displaced spherical source and for oblate ejecta. We validate them against Monte Carlo (MC) radiative transfer and derive geometric approximations to the peak-luminosity anisotropy. For a displaced spherical source, the quasi-steady approximation, equivalent to stationary diffusion in frozen ejecta, gives $L_{\mathrm p}(θ)/L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}\simeq1+(17/8)z_{\mathrm{off}}\cosθ$, where $z_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the displacement in units of the ejecta radius, $θ$ the viewing angle from the displacement axis, and $L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}$ the angle-averaged peak. This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

entry.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
entry.summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.
entry.arxiv:comment: 39 pages, 3 figures, v2: rewriting of Sec. 3.1, correction of typos, and improved wording

entry.title: A First-Order Gauge Approach to de Sitter General Relativity
entry.summary: We propose a first-order gauge formulation of de Sitter relativity in which the pseudo-radius l(x) is promoted to a spacetime field, locally breaking SO(4,1) to SO(3,1). Here, l(x) is a geometric compensator and dl(x) the associated order parameter. This modifies the Strong Equivalence Principle: the local vacuum follows the matter distribution instead of remaining fixed, while the propagating degrees of freedom of General Relativity are unchanged. At fixed l(x), the action is SO(3,1)-gauge invariant, but varying l(x) destroys covariance under the full translational sector of SO(4,1). Through the Inonu-Wigner contraction, abstract generators become explicit spacetime transformations, yielding nonlinear Killing vectors in both the macroscopic l tends to infinity and microscopic l tends to 0 limits. The generalized Noether theorem gives a unified energy-momentum current coupling the standard tensor to the proper conformal matter current. It vanishes identically without matter, causing the asymptotic extinction of local vacuum energy and the decay of the background to Minkowski spacetime. Independent variations yield the coupled de Sitter field equations, and we algebraically prove their equivalence to the tensorial splitting on the coordinate manifold. Gauge Bianchi identities further show that Lambda(x) is an intrinsic source of spacetime torsion, consistently identifying it with the local order parameter of the symmetry breaking. The cosmological constant problem is therefore recast, not numerically solved: deriving the decay of Lambda(x) from early-universe densities to its observed value remains future work.

entry.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
entry.summary: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
entry.summary: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.
entry.arxiv:comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release". 15 pages, 5 figures

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): VIS processing and data products
entry.summary: This paper describes the characteristics of the Euclid visible imager (VIS) data delivered as part of the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). This data set contains 42092 calibrated frames. Validated nominal exposures cover 2092 deg$^2$ of sky. We outline the minor changes made to the VIS processing function (PF) since previous releases. For the wide survey, the photometric and astrometric accuracy of the reference stellar sample $(18.5 < I_{\rm E} < 19.8)$ is excellent. The internal and external astrometric dispersions are 0.08 and 0.18 mas, respectively, at the quadrant level, and 3.4 and 5.6 mas at the source level. The corresponding internal and external photometric dispersions are 0.76 and 1.4 mmag at the quadrant level, and 11 and 25 mmag at the source level. We characterise remaining astrometric and photometric systematic effects: focal-plane-dependent variations; time-dependent photometric offsets; and colour-dependent centroid shifts. The noise floor in the deepest VIS images appears to be set by the extended diffuse light of faint galaxies. Globally, the DR1 VIS data meet pre-launch mission requirements and the 42092 images it contains provide our first substantial look at the sky as seen by VIS.
entry.arxiv:comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

entry.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
entry.summary: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
entry.summary: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.
entry.arxiv:comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Submitted to A&A. Catalogue: https://euclid-eclipse-lenses.org ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19654904

entry.title: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
entry.summary: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ketΩ$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
entry.summary: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.
entry.arxiv:comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, submitted to A&A. Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
entry.summary: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.
entry.arxiv:comment: 28 pages. Submitted to A&A as part of the Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

entry.title: Measuring the growth index in the $w_0w_a$CDM background
entry.summary: We produce a measurement of the growth index, $γ$, which is used to parametrize the scale-independent growth of linear matter perturbations on sub-horizon scales, for the $w_0w_a$CDM background model. In 2023, assuming the $Λ$CDM background, the value $γ=0.633^{+0.025}_{-0.024}$ was obtained, excluding the General Relativity value of $γ=0.55$ at $3.7σ$ statistical significance. In 2025, an analysis of baryon acoustic oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopy Instrument (DESI) demonstrated a preference for a dynamical dark energy over the cosmological constant model, $Λ$, ranging from $2.8-4.2σ$, depending on the external datasets used. Therefore it is important to determine how the $γ$ measurement is modified in the context of dynamical dark energy and verify whether the tension with the expected theoretical value persists. Considering data from Planck cosmic microwave background anisotropies, $fσ_{8}$, baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI and supernova Ia luminosity distances from Phanteon+, we find $γ_{w_0w_a}=0.633\pm0.024$, essentially the same value found for the $Λ$CDM background. This result excludes the General Relativity value for the $w_0w_a$CDM background evolution at $3.4σ$ level. We also show that the $γ$ posteriors across many datasets combinations are consistent with each other and that main driver of the "$γ$ tension" is the $fσ_{8}$ dataset.

entry.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
entry.summary: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 πf(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

entry.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) D: Photometric redshifts and the first census of strong lenses in the galaxy evolution framework
entry.summary: The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.
